_readme: Consumer Rights Wizard + Rights Checker + Timeline Generator config — the ONLY file you edit to change any of the three tools. decision-tree-core.js reads 'problems', 'countries' and 'combinations' and renders screens 1-2 dynamically (no problem/country-specific code); each page supplies its own screen-3 renderer. TO ADD A PROBLEM: add its name to 'problems' and add a 'Problem|Country' entry for each country. TO ADD A COUNTRY (e.g. 'EU'): add it to 'countries' and add a 'Problem|EU' entry for each problem. Each combination may carry: directory, article, tool, template (any may be null — the Wizard result screen skips null cards); 'rights' (Refund/Replacement/Repair/Chargeback/Escalation booleans, shown by the Rights Checker); and 'timeline' (ordered steps with a label and days_from_start integer, shown by the Timeline Generator) plus 'timeline_recommended' (true when the steps are practical recommendations rather than statutory deadlines, so the UI can label them honestly). A right/deadline is set only when supported by the linked article/resource. All urls are site-absolute (leading slash).

timeline.label: Call your bank immediately to try to freeze or recall the funds
Report to Scamwatch, and contact IDCARE if your ID was exposed
Log it with ReportCyber (cyber.gov.au) for a reference number
Escalate to AFCA if the bank won't act (including the receiving bank)

directory.name: EU Banking Dispute & Payment Fraud Resources

article.title: How to File a Complaint Against Your Bank in the EU

timeline.label: Send a formal complaint to your bank, titled to invoke the Payment Services Directive
Bank must give a final written response (15 business days)
Exceptional extended deadline if the bank has notified you (35 business days)
No response, or unsatisfactory reply? Escalate to FIN-NET

directory.name: EU Subscription Cancellation & Renewal Law Resources

article.title: How to Cancel a Subscription Under EU Law: What "Easy Exit" Actually Covers Today

timeline.label: Check whether you're still in your 14-day EU-wide withdrawal window
If not, check whether your country has a specific cancellation-button law (e.g. Germany, France) or an unnotified-renewal notice rule
Send a formal cancellation/refund demand citing the correct basis for your country and scenario
If the company keeps billing, revoke the payment mandate directly through your bank (PSD2)

article.title: Bank Spoofing Scams: Your Refund Rights Under PSD2 in the EU

timeline.label: Report the scam to your bank/payment provider and request a refund for the unauthorised transaction
Your PSP must refund by the end of the next business day unless it suspects fraud (PSD2, Article 73)
If the trader/scammer is in another EU country, also report it to ECC-Net
If refused or delayed, escalate via FIN-NET to your national ombudsman

directory.name: TIO — Resolve an Individual Phone/Internet Dispute (Australia)

article.title: The TIO Mandate: Force ISPs to Cancel Contracts and Waive Termination Fees

timeline.label: Contact your provider in writing to cancel, or dispute the early termination fee
Give the provider a reasonable window to resolve it directly (TCP Code timeframes)
Escalate to the TIO if it's unresolved or ignored

directory.name: Australia Post — Lost or Damaged Parcel Complaints

article.title: Australia Post's $100 Default Cover, and Why Extra Cover Claims Get Rejected

timeline.label: Contact the retailer (not the courier) in writing
Lodge a complaint with Australia Post/StarTrack if the delivery itself failed
Escalate to the Postal Industry Ombudsman if unresolved (only accepted after the carrier complaint above)
Escalate to a chargeback with your bank if still unresolved

directory.name: European Consumer Centres Network (ECC-Net) — Delivery Disputes

article.title: ECC-Net: Free Cross-Border Mediation for a Delivery Dispute With an EU Seller

timeline.label: Contact the seller in writing — the seller is responsible for delivery, not the courier (Article 20)
Give the seller a reasonable additional deadline to deliver (Article 18)
If still missed, cancel the order and demand a refund
If the seller is in another EU country and refuses, escalate to ECC-Net for free mediation

article.title: Wage Theft Is Now a Crime in Australia: Restaurant Award Compliance Guide

timeline.label: Request the unpaid wages/entitlements in writing from your employer
Check your correct rate against the Fair Work Pay Calculator
Give a final deadline before escalating
Lodge a dispute with the Fair Work Commission if still unresolved

article.title: The EU Platform Work Directive: Rebuttable Presumption of Employment

timeline.label: Document your working pattern and any signs of employer control (relevant to the rebuttable presumption)
Send a written request to the platform/employer for reclassification or unpaid entitlements
If ignored, escalate to your national labour inspectorate, or the European Labour Authority for cross-border cases

directory.name: UK CAA — Am I Entitled to Compensation?

article.title: UK261 Consumer Framework: Passenger Entitlements, CAA Oversight, and ADR Audits

tool.name: Flight Disruption Compensation & Reimbursement Letter Generator

article.title: Automatic Refunds and the DOT Rules for Significant Flight Delays

tool.name: Flight Disruption Compensation & Reimbursement Letter Generator

timeline.label: Request a refund from the airline for a cancelled or significantly changed flight
Airline must issue the refund within 7 business days for credit-card purchases (DOT automatic refund rule)
If refused, file a complaint with the DOT's Aviation Consumer Protection division

article.title: Flight Delayed in Australia: What Are Your Rights?

tool.name: Flight Disruption Compensation & Reimbursement Letter Generator

timeline.label: Contact the airline directly and insist on a cash refund (not just a voucher) if the disruption is severe
Keep every receipt for meals, transport and accommodation caused by the disruption
Escalate to the Airline Customer Advocate if the airline won't budge (covers only Jetstar, Qantas, Rex and Virgin Australia)
For a substantive ACL claim, go to your state/territory consumer protection agency instead

article.title: Flight Delayed? EU261 Compensation Explained

tool.name: EU261 Flight Delay/Cancellation Compensation Claim Generator

timeline.label: Submit a compensation claim directly to the airline, citing EU261
Give the airline a reasonable window to respond before escalating (enforcement timelines vary by member state)
Escalate to your national enforcement body, or ECC-Net for a cross-border claim

article.title: APP Fraud Reimbursement and Crypto: Why the UK's Mandatory Refund Rule Often Doesn't Cover Crypto Investment Scams

timeline.label: Report to your bank/exchange immediately and request a freeze
Report to Action Fraud
Ask your bank about APP fraud reimbursement — be aware crypto investment scams are frequently excluded from the mandatory scheme
If you paid by card, pursue a Section 75/chargeback claim instead

directory.name: US — FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)

article.title: Crypto ATM Scams: Why Regulators Are Cracking Down on These Machines

timeline.label: Stop all further transfers and contact the exchange to attempt a freeze
Report to the FBI's IC3 and the FTC
If funded by card, dispute the charge with your card issuer
Follow up or escalate if unresolved

article.title: Financial Liability & Crypto Transactions in Task Scams under the ACL

timeline.label: Contact your bank immediately and report the transaction
Report to ReportCyber and Scamwatch
If funded by card, dispute the charge with your bank
Escalate to AFCA if your bank won't act

article.title: The EU's Transfer of Funds Regulation: What Actually Changed for Your Crypto Transfers

timeline.label: Report to your bank/payment provider immediately and request a freeze
Report to your national police or cybercrime unit (Europol supports cross-border cases but doesn't take individual reports directly)
If funded by card, pursue a chargeback through your card issuer
Follow up with your national regulator if the platform itself was unlicensed

directory.name: UK — Office of the Independent Adjudicator (OIA)

article.title: Reclaiming a University Tuition Deposit: Your Rights Under UK Consumer Law

timeline.label: Request your deposit/tuition refund from the university in writing
Give the university a reasonable window to respond via its own complaints process
Escalate to the OIA once the university's internal complaints process is exhausted
Deadline to refer to the OIA (12 months from the university's final Completion of Procedures letter)

directory.name: US — Federal Trade Commission (Education & Bootcamp Claims)

article.title: Fake Job Placement Rates: How Bootcamps Inflate Outcomes and What the FTC Requires

timeline.label: File a complaint with the FTC about the deceptive job-placement claims
Request a refund directly from the school/bootcamp in writing, citing the misrepresentation
If paid by card, dispute the charge with your card issuer
Check your state's specific vocational-school refund law for an additional deadline

article.title: Your Australian College Closed: How the Tuition Protection Service Actually Works

timeline.label: Contact your provider in writing about the closure or non-delivery of your course
Contact the Tuition Protection Service — it should place you in a replacement course or arrange a refund
Follow up if the replacement course or refund isn't arranged

article.title: The 14-Day Right of Withdrawal for Online Courses in the EU

timeline.label: Exercise the 14-day right of withdrawal in writing, if still within the window
If the window has passed, contact the provider directly citing the withdrawal right and request a refund
If refused, check your national consumer protection authority via the European Education Area

article.title: How to File an FCC Complaint About Your Telecom Provider

timeline.label: Contact your provider directly to request a billing credit for a verified outage or billing error
If unresolved, file a complaint with the FCC's Consumer Complaint Center
Your provider is legally required to respond in writing within 30 days
If billed by card, dispute it under the Fair Credit Billing Act (60-day window from the bill)

article.title: How to Escalate an Unresolved Energy or Telecom Complaint to the Ombudsman

timeline.label: Raise the billing/service issue with your provider in writing
Check whether you're owed automatic compensation (e.g. Ofcom's scheme for broadband delays/faults)
Give your provider a reasonable window to respond before pursuing ADR (commonly 8 weeks)
Escalate to the correct ADR scheme for your issue — Communications Ombudsman/CISAS for telecom, Energy Ombudsman for energy/water

directory.name: EWON — Energy & Water Ombudsman (NSW; check your state's scheme)

article.title: Sky-High Energy or Water Bill? How to Get a Faulty Meter Tested in Australia

timeline.label: Request a meter test/billing review from your provider in writing
Keep your own photographed meter readings as independent evidence
Give the provider a reasonable window to respond
Escalate to your state's Energy & Water Ombudsman (EWON/EWOV/EWOQ etc. — check which covers you), or the TIO for a telecom issue

article.title: Challenging Estimated Energy Bills in the EU: Your Rights Under the Electricity Market Directive

timeline.label: Request an actual-usage bill correction from your provider, citing the Electricity Market Directive
Give the provider a reasonable window to respond (national timelines vary by member state)
Escalate to your national energy regulator/ombudsman, or ECC-Net for a cross-border dispute

article.title: Denied Entry With a Service Animal? Restaurant and Hotel Rules Under the ADA

timeline.label: Document exactly what happened, including staff/manager names if possible
Request a resolution directly from the restaurant or hotel manager
File a complaint with the FTC (or the DOJ specifically for an ADA violation)
If billed for a service not rendered as described, dispute the charge with your card issuer

article.title: Natasha's Law: Allergen Labelling Rules for Prepacked-for-Direct-Sale Food

timeline.label: Raise the issue directly with the restaurant/venue in writing, citing the allergen information you were given
Give the venue a reasonable window to respond
Contact Citizens Advice for guidance on your next step if unresolved
Report a labelling/allergen failure to your local authority's Trading Standards or Environmental Health team

article.title: Restaurant Allergen Disclosure Under EU Regulation 1169/2011 (FIC Regulation)

timeline.label: Raise the issue directly with the restaurant/venue in writing, citing Regulation (EU) 1169/2011
Give the venue a reasonable window to respond (national timelines vary by member state)
If unresolved and the business is in another EU country, escalate via ECC-Net

directory.name: FDA MedWatch — Report a Supplement Side Effect

article.title: How to Report a Supplement Side Effect to the FDA (MedWatch)

timeline.label: Stop taking the product and seek medical attention if needed

Request a refund directly from the seller, citing the safety issue
If billed by card and the seller refuses, dispute the charge with your card issuer

directory.name: MHRA Yellow Card — Report an Unsafe Supplement (UK)

article.title: How to Report a Supplement Side Effect via the MHRA Yellow Card Scheme

timeline.label: Stop taking the product and seek medical attention if needed
Report the reaction via the MHRA Yellow Card scheme
Request a refund from the retailer, citing the Consumer Rights Act (satisfactory quality)
Escalate to Trading Standards if refused

directory.name: TGA / Product Safety Australia — Safety Reporting

article.title: How to Report a Supplement Side Effect to the TGA (Australia)

timeline.label: Stop taking the product and seek medical attention if needed
Report to the TGA (Report a Problem) and check the DAEN database
Request a refund or replacement from the retailer under the ACL
Escalate to Product Safety Australia (ACCC) or your state consumer protection agency if refused
